original_value: As classical planning is known to be computationally hard, no single planner is expected to work well across many planning domains. One solution to this problem is to use online portfolio planners that select a planner for a given task. These portfolios perform a classification task, a well-known and wellresearched task in the field of machine learning. The classification is usually performed using a representation of planning tasks with a collection of hand-crafted statistical features. Recent techniques in machine learning that are based on automatic extraction of features have not been employed yet due to the lack of suitable representations of planning tasks.In this work, we alleviate this barrier. We suggest representing planning tasks by images, allowing to exploit arguably one of the most commonly used and best developed techniques in deep learning. We explore some of the questions that inevitably rise when applying such a technique, and present various ways of building practically useful online portfoliobased planners. An evidence of the usefulness of our proposed technique is a planner that won the cost-optimal track of the International Planning Competition 2018.

result.paraphrase: Because classical planning is computationally difficult, no one planner can be expected to perform well across a wide range of planning domains. A common remedy is to use online portfolio planners that choose a planner for each task. These portfolios carry out a classification problem, a familiar and well-studied area in machine learning. This classification is typically based on representing planning tasks with hand-crafted statistical features. Recent machine learning methods that automatically extract features have not been used yet because suitable representations of planning tasks are lacking. In this work, we remove that obstacle. We propose encoding planning tasks as images, making it possible to use one of deep learning’s most common and most mature techniques. We examine several questions that naturally arise when applying such a method and present multiple ways to build practically useful online portfolio-based planners. The value of our approach is demonstrated by a planner that won the cost-optimal track of the International Planning Competition 2018.
